## Introduction

In class we built k-means one idea at a time: the **within-cluster variation**
we want to make small, **Lloyd's algorithm** that makes it smaller step by step,
and **hierarchical clustering**, which does not need $K$ in advance. This lab
lets you *see* each idea on simulated data.

There is no code to run here. Each section is a small **Shiny app** that runs
in your browser (via [Shinylive](https://posit-dev.github.io/r-shinylive/) and
webR), so you do not need to install R. The first app takes 10–30 seconds to
start while R and the packages download. The other apps start faster.

On simulated data we know the true groups, so we can check every answer. The
real data analysis, on thyroid patients, is in
[Lab 2](class7_lab2.html){target="_blank"}.

## 1. Lloyd's algorithm, one step at a time

The slides give the algorithm in two steps:

1. Randomly assign a number from 1 to $K$ to each observation.
2. Repeat until the assignments stop changing:
   a. **Update:** for each cluster, compute the centroid (the mean of its
      points).
   b. **Assign:** move each observation to the cluster with the closest
      centroid.

Click **Next step** to do one half-step at a time. The title says which step
just happened. The right panel tracks the within-cluster sum of squares (WSS),
$\sum_k \sum_{i \in C_k} \lVert x_i - \mu_k \rVert^2$, after every
half-step. Here $\mu_k$ is the current centroid of cluster $k$ (the big X). Click **New random start** to begin again from a different random
assignment.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 660
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)
ctr <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 0.5), c(1.5, 3.5))
pts <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(150, ctr[rep(1:3, each = 50), 1], 0.8),
                  x2 = rnorm(150, ctr[rep(1:3, each = 50), 2], 0.8))
X <- as.matrix(pts)
pal <- c("#3B4992", "#EE0000", "#008B45", "#631879", "#E69F00")

centroids <- function(cl, K, old = NULL) {
  t(sapply(1:K, function(k) {
    if (any(cl == k)) colMeans(X[cl == k, , drop = FALSE])
    else if (!is.null(old)) old[k, ] else colMeans(X)   # keep an empty cluster's old centroid
  }))
}
wss_of <- function(cl, cen) sum((X - cen[cl, ])^2)

ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    sliderInput("K", "number of clusters K", min = 2, max = 5, value = 3),
    actionButton("restart", "New random start"),
    actionButton("step", "Next step", class = "btn-primary"),
    actionButton("finish", "Run to the end")
  ),
  layout_columns(col_widths = c(7, 5),
    plotOutput("scatter", height = "560px"),
    plotOutput("trace", height = "560px"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  st <- reactiveValues()
  init <- function() {
    K <- input$K
    st$cl <- sample(1:K, nrow(X), replace = TRUE)       # step 1: random labels
    st$cen <- NULL
    st$next_is <- "update"
    st$iter <- 0
    st$msg <- "Start: random labels, no centroids yet"
    st$hist <- data.frame(step = 0, wss = wss_of(st$cl, centroids(st$cl, K)),
                          kind = "start")
    st$done <- FALSE
  }
  half_step <- function() {
    if (st$done) return()
    K <- input$K
    if (st$next_is == "update") {
      st$cen <- centroids(st$cl, K, st$cen)
      st$iter <- st$iter + 1
      st$msg <- sprintf("Iteration %d (a): update centroids", st$iter)
      st$next_is <- "assign"
      kind <- "update"
    } else {
      d <- sapply(1:K, function(k) colSums((t(X) - st$cen[k, ])^2))
      new_cl <- max.col(-d, ties.method = "first")
      changed <- sum(new_cl != st$cl)
      st$cl <- new_cl
      st$msg <- sprintf("Iteration %d (b): %d point(s) moved", st$iter, changed)
      st$next_is <- "update"
      if (changed == 0) { st$done <- TRUE; st$msg <- sprintf("Converged after %d iterations", st$iter) }
      kind <- "assign"
    }
    cen <- if (is.null(st$cen)) centroids(st$cl, K) else st$cen
    st$hist <- rbind(st$hist, data.frame(step = nrow(st$hist), wss = wss_of(st$cl, cen), kind = kind))
  }
  observeEvent(list(input$K, input$restart), init())
  observeEvent(input$step, half_step())
  observeEvent(input$finish, { for (i in 1:100) { if (st$done) break; half_step() } })

  output$scatter <- renderPlot({
    req(st$cl)
    d <- cbind(pts, cluster = factor(st$cl, levels = 1:input$K))
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(x1, x2, colour = cluster)) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
      coord_equal() +
      labs(title = st$msg,
           subtitle = sprintf("WSS = %.1f", tail(st$hist$wss, 1))) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    if (!is.null(st$cen)) {
      cd <- data.frame(x1 = st$cen[, 1], x2 = st$cen[, 2],
                       cluster = factor(1:input$K, levels = 1:input$K))
      p <- p + geom_point(data = cd, shape = 4, size = 9, stroke = 2.5)
    }
    p
  }, res = 96)

  output$trace <- renderPlot({
    req(st$hist)
    ggplot(st$hist, aes(step, wss)) +
      geom_line(colour = "grey50") +
      geom_point(aes(shape = kind), size = 3) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(start = 15, update = 16, assign = 17),
                         name = NULL) +
      labs(x = "half-step", y = "WSS", title = "WSS after each half-step") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  }, res = 96)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Things to notice:

- **The first update moves every centroid to the middle.** Random labels mix
  all groups, so every cluster mean starts near the overall mean. The centroids
  then separate over the next few iterations.
- **WSS never goes up.** Each half-step can only lower it, or leave it the
  same. The update step puts each centroid at the point that minimizes the sum
  of squares for its cluster. The assign step moves a point only when that
  makes its own term smaller. This is why the algorithm must stop.
- **Most of the gain comes early.** The first two or three iterations do most
  of the work. The last iterations move a few points near the borders.
- Set $K = 5$ on data with three groups. The algorithm still runs and still
  converges. k-means always returns $K$ clusters, even when $K$ is wrong.

## 2. Bad starts and local minima

Lloyd's algorithm stops when no single step helps. That is a **local**
minimum. It is not always the best possible clustering. These data have five
groups: two pairs on the left and one group on the right. The app runs
`kmeans()` with $K = 5$ from the random start you pick.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 640
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)
ctr <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(3, 0), c(0, 5), c(3, 5), c(8, 2.5))
X <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(i)
  cbind(rnorm(40, ctr[i, 1], 0.6), rnorm(40, ctr[i, 2], 0.6))))
colnames(X) <- c("x1", "x2")
best <- kmeans(X, 5, nstart = 50)$tot.withinss
pal <- c("#3B4992", "#EE0000", "#008B45", "#631879", "#E69F00")

ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    sliderInput("seed", "random start number", min = 1, max = 30, value = 1,
                step = 1, animate = animationOptions(interval = 1500)),
    radioButtons("nstart", "nstart (starts per run, best one kept)",
                 choices = c(1, 5, 25), selected = 1, inline = TRUE)
  ),
  plotOutput("plot", height = "560px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    set.seed(input$seed)
    km <- kmeans(X, 5, nstart = as.integer(input$nstart))
    worse <- 100 * (km$tot.withinss / best - 1)
    d <- data.frame(X, cluster = factor(km$cluster))
    cd <- data.frame(km$centers, cluster = factor(1:5))
    ggplot(d, aes(x1, x2, colour = cluster)) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
      geom_point(data = cd, shape = 4, size = 9, stroke = 2.5) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
      coord_equal() +
      labs(title = sprintf("WSS = %.1f   (best possible: %.1f)", km$tot.withinss, best),
           subtitle = if (worse > 1) sprintf("Local minimum: %.0f%% worse than the best", worse)
                      else "This run found the best clustering") +
      theme_bw(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }, res = 96)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Press ▶ under the slider to step through the 30 starts. With `nstart = 1`:

- **20 of the 30 starts stop at a local minimum.** A typical bad answer puts
  two centroids in one group and makes one centroid cover two groups.
- With `nstart = 5`, 2 of the 30 runs are still bad. With `nstart = 25`, none
  are.

A local minimum looks like a normal result. `kmeans()` gives no warning. The
only protection is many starts. Use `nstart = 25` or more, and set a seed so
that other people get the same clusters.

## 3. Units change the clusters

k-means uses Euclidean distance. A variable with a large spread contributes
large distances, so it dominates. Below are 200 simulated patients, half with
diabetes. Two lab values were measured:

- **HbA1c** (%), which differs between the groups
- **total cholesterol**, which does **not** differ between the groups

Cholesterol can be reported in mg/dL or in mmol/L (1 mmol/L = 38.67 mg/dL).
The patients and the measurements stay the same. Only the units change.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 640
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)
n <- 100
group <- factor(rep(c("no diabetes", "diabetes"), each = n),
                levels = c("no diabetes", "diabetes"))
chol_mgdl <- rnorm(2 * n, 200, 40)                     # same in both groups
a1c <- c(rnorm(n, 5.4, 0.35), rnorm(n, 7.6, 0.6))    # differs between groups

ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    radioButtons("units", "cholesterol units",
                 choices = c("mg/dL", "mmol/L"), selected = "mg/dL"),
    checkboxInput("std", "standardize both variables first", FALSE),
    checkboxInput("equal", "draw both axes on the same scale (what k-means sees)", FALSE)
  ),
  plotOutput("plot", height = "560px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    chol <- if (input$units == "mg/dL") chol_mgdl else chol_mgdl / 38.67
    X <- cbind(chol = chol, a1c = a1c)
    Xfit <- if (input$std) scale(X) else X
    set.seed(42)
    cl <- kmeans(Xfit, 2, nstart = 25)$cluster
    agree <- max(mean(cl == as.integer(group)), mean(cl != as.integer(group)))
    d <- data.frame(Xfit, cluster = factor(cl), group = group)
    p <- ggplot(d, aes(chol, a1c, colour = cluster, shape = group)) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c("#3B4992", "#EE0000")) +
      labs(x = if (input$std) "cholesterol (standardized)" else paste0("cholesterol (", input$units, ")"),
           y = if (input$std) "HbA1c (standardized)" else "HbA1c (%)",
           title = sprintf("k-means, K = 2: %.0f%% of patients matched to their group",
                           100 * agree)) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    if (input$equal) {
      # same units on both axes: centre the y-axis on the data, with the x-axis span
      span <- diff(range(d$chol)) / 2
      p <- p + coord_equal(xlim = range(d$chol), ylim = mean(d$a1c) + c(-span, span))
    }
    p
  }, res = 96)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Try the four combinations:

| cholesterol units | standardize | patients matched |
|---|---|---|
| mg/dL | no | 52% (no better than chance) |
| mmol/L | no | 100% |
| mg/dL | yes | 99% |
| mmol/L | yes | 99% |

- In mg/dL, cholesterol has an SD near 40, and HbA1c has an SD near 1.2.
  Tick "same scale" to see what k-means sees: a long horizontal band. k-means
  cuts the band in half **along cholesterol**, the variable that has no
  information.
- In mmol/L, the cholesterol SD is about 1, so HbA1c can be seen. The clusters
  now follow diabetes status.
- **Standardizing makes the answer the same for any units.** This is why the
  slides say: *always center and scale*.

## 4. Choosing $K$

Three tools from class and Lab 2:

- **Elbow:** WSS against $K$. Look for the bend.
- **Silhouette:** for each point, compare the mean distance to its own cluster
  ($a$) with the mean distance to the nearest other cluster ($b$):
  $s = (b - a)/\max(a, b)$. Choose the $K$ with the largest mean $s$. Lab 2
  explains it in full.
- **Gap statistic:** compare $\log(\text{WSS})$ with its value on reference
  data with no clusters. Choose the smallest $K$ whose gap is within one
  standard error of the next gap.

Pick a data set, change the spread of the groups, and see which $K$ each tool
picks. The left panel shows k-means with the $K$ from the slider. The gap
statistic uses $B = 20$ reference sets, so give each change a few seconds.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 760
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)

make_data <- function(type, spread) {
  set.seed(42)
  if (type == "no groups") return(cbind(x1 = rnorm(150), x2 = rnorm(150)))
  Kt <- if (type == "3 groups") 3 else 4
  ang <- 2 * pi * (1:Kt) / Kt
  y <- rep(1:Kt, each = 50)
  cbind(x1 = rnorm(50 * Kt, 3 * cos(ang)[y], spread),
        x2 = rnorm(50 * Kt, 3 * sin(ang)[y], spread))
}
pal <- c("#3B4992", "#EE0000", "#008B45", "#631879", "#E69F00",
         "#008280", "#BB0021", "#5F559B")

ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    radioButtons("type", "data", choices = c("3 groups", "4 groups", "no groups")),
    sliderInput("spread", "spread of each group (SD)", min = 0.5, max = 1.5,
                value = 0.5, step = 0.25),
    sliderInput("K", "K for the left panel", min = 1, max = 8, value = 3)
  ),
  layout_columns(col_widths = c(6, 6),
    plotOutput("scatter", height = "330px"),
    plotOutput("elbow", height = "330px"),
    plotOutput("sil", height = "330px"),
    plotOutput("gap", height = "330px"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  X <- reactive(make_data(input$type, input$spread))
  fits <- reactive({
    lapply(1:8, function(k) { set.seed(42); kmeans(X(), k, nstart = 10) })
  })
  sil <- reactive({
    d <- dist(X())
    sapply(2:8, function(k) mean(silhouette(fits()[[k]]$cluster, d)[, "sil_width"]))
  })
  gap <- reactive({
    set.seed(42)
    clusGap(X(), kmeans, K.max = 8, B = 20, nstart = 10)$Tab
  })
  base <- theme_bw(base_size = 14)
  output$scatter <- renderPlot({
    d <- data.frame(X(), cluster = factor(fits()[[input$K]]$cluster))
    ggplot(d, aes(x1, x2, colour = cluster)) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = pal) + coord_equal() +
      labs(title = sprintf("k-means with K = %d", input$K)) +
      base + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }, res = 96)
  output$elbow <- renderPlot({
    d <- data.frame(k = 1:8, wss = sapply(fits(), `[[`, "tot.withinss"))
    ggplot(d, aes(k, wss)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
      labs(x = "K", y = "WSS", title = "Elbow: look for the bend") + base
  }, res = 96)
  output$sil <- renderPlot({
    d <- data.frame(k = 2:8, s = sil())
    best <- d$k[which.max(d$s)]
    ggplot(d, aes(k, s)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
      geom_point(data = d[d$k == best, ], colour = "#EE0000", size = 4) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8, limits = c(1, 8)) +
      labs(x = "K", y = "average silhouette",
           title = sprintf("Silhouette picks K = %d", best)) + base
  }, res = 96)
  output$gap <- renderPlot({
    g <- gap()
    best <- maxSE(g[, "gap"], g[, "SE.sim"], method = "firstSEmax")
    d <- data.frame(k = 1:8, g)
    ggplot(d, aes(k, gap)) + geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = gap - SE.sim, ymax = gap + SE.sim), width = 0.2) +
      geom_point(data = d[d$k == best, ], colour = "#EE0000", size = 4) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
      labs(x = "K", y = "Gap(K)", title = sprintf("Gap statistic picks K = %d", best)) + base
  }, res = 96)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

What the tools pick:

| data | spread | silhouette | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 groups | 0.5 to 1.0 | 3 | 3 |
| 3 groups | 1.25 or 1.5 | 3 | **1** |
| 4 groups | 0.5 to 1.25 | 4 | 4 |
| 4 groups | 1.5 | 4 | **1** |
| no groups | — | **4** | 1 |

- **Well-separated groups are easy.** All three tools agree.
- **When the groups overlap, the gap statistic gives up first.** At spread 1.5
  (1.25 for three groups) the groups touch, and the data no longer look very different from the
  no-cluster reference. The gap says $K = 1$.
- **The silhouette cannot say "no clusters".** It starts at $K = 2$, so on data
  with no groups it still picks a $K$ (here 4). The gap statistic correctly
  says $K = 1$. The two tools fail in opposite directions.
- **The elbow is the least precise.** With overlap or no groups, the curve has
  no clear bend.

## 5. Shapes that k-means cannot find

k-means puts each point with its closest centroid. So every cluster is a
convex region around a centre, and the border between two clusters is a
straight line halfway between their centroids. When the true groups have
another shape, k-means cannot find them. Hierarchical clustering with a
different linkage sometimes can.

Pick a shape and a method. $K$ is set to the true number of groups. The title
gives the share of points in a cluster that matches their true group.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 640
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)

make <- function(type) {
  set.seed(42)
  switch(type,
    "round, equal" = { y <- rep(1:3, each = 70)
      data.frame(x1 = rnorm(210, c(0, 4, 2)[y], 0.7), x2 = rnorm(210, c(0, 0, 3.5)[y], 0.7), g = y) },
    "unequal sizes" = { y <- rep(1:2, c(250, 30))
      data.frame(x1 = rnorm(280, c(0, 4.2)[y], c(1.2, 0.4)[y]), x2 = rnorm(280, 0, c(1.2, 0.4)[y]), g = y) },
    "elongated" = { y <- rep(1:2, each = 100)
      u <- rnorm(200, 0, 3); v <- rnorm(200, c(-1.1, 1.1)[y], 0.35)   # long along u, apart along v
      data.frame(x1 = (u - v) / sqrt(2), x2 = (u + v) / sqrt(2), g = y) },   # tilt by 45 degrees
    "rings" = { y <- rep(1:2, c(80, 160)); th <- runif(240, 0, 2 * pi)
      r <- c(1, 4)[y] + rnorm(240, 0, 0.25)
      data.frame(x1 = r * cos(th), x2 = r * sin(th), g = y) },
    "moons" = { y <- rep(1:2, each = 100); th <- runif(200, 0, pi)
      data.frame(x1 = ifelse(y == 1, cos(th), 1 - cos(th)) + rnorm(200, 0, 0.07),
                 x2 = ifelse(y == 1, sin(th), 0.5 - sin(th)) + rnorm(200, 0, 0.07), g = y) })
}
agree <- function(cl, g) { t <- table(cl, g); sum(apply(t, 1, max)) / length(g) }

ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    radioButtons("type", "true groups",
                 choices = c("round, equal", "unequal sizes", "elongated", "rings", "moons")),
    radioButtons("method", "method",
                 choices = c("k-means", "hierarchical: complete", "hierarchical: average",
                             "hierarchical: single", "hierarchical: Ward"))
  ),
  plotOutput("plot", height = "560px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    d <- make(input$type)
    X <- as.matrix(d[, c("x1", "x2")])
    K <- length(unique(d$g))
    cl <- if (input$method == "k-means") {
      set.seed(42); kmeans(X, K, nstart = 25)$cluster
    } else {
      link <- c("hierarchical: complete" = "complete", "hierarchical: average" = "average",
                "hierarchical: single" = "single", "hierarchical: Ward" = "ward.D2")[input$method]
      cutree(hclust(dist(X), method = link), K)
    }
    d$cluster <- factor(cl)
    ggplot(d, aes(x1, x2, colour = cluster)) +
      geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c("#3B4992", "#EE0000", "#008B45")) +
      coord_equal() +
      labs(title = sprintf("%s, K = %d: %.0f%% matched", input$method, K, 100 * agree(cl, d$g))) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }, res = 96)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Points matched to their true group:

| shape | k-means | complete | average | single | Ward |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| round, equal | 100% | 100% | 100% | 67% | 100% |
| unequal sizes | 89% | 89% | 89% | 89% | 100% |
| elongated | 56% | 52% | 50% | 50% | 52% |
| rings | 67% | 72% | 67% | **100%** | 68% |
| moons | 76% | 87% | 74% | **100%** | 87% |

- **Round, equal groups are what k-means is built for.** Every method except
  single linkage does well.
- **Unequal sizes:** the k-means border sits halfway between the two centroids.
  The large, wide group reaches past that border, so k-means gives some of its
  points to the small group.
- **Elongated groups defeat every method here.** Each group is a long, thin,
  tilted band. Cutting across both bands, into two halves along their length,
  gives a WSS of 905. The true split gives 1716. k-means minimizes WSS, so it
  picks the wrong cut. Scaling does not help: the bands are tilted, so both
  variables have the same spread already. (Class 8's Gaussian mixture models
  can fit long, tilted clusters.)
- **Rings and moons: single linkage wins.** Single linkage joins two groups
  when their two **closest** points are near. It follows a chain of near
  neighbours around a curve. The same behaviour makes it fail on round groups:
  a few points between groups are enough to chain them together.

## 6. Reading a dendrogram

Hierarchical clustering builds a tree. Each merge is drawn at the height of the
distance between the two groups it joins. Cutting the tree with a horizontal
line gives the clusters: each branch that the line crosses is one cluster.

These 30 points come from three groups. The numbers on the points match the
leaves of the tree.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 640
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)
ctr <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(3, 0.5), c(1.2, 3))
d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(30, ctr[rep(1:3, each = 10), 1], 0.55),
                x2 = rnorm(30, ctr[rep(1:3, each = 10), 2], 0.55),
                id = 1:30)
D <- dist(d[, c("x1", "x2")])
pal <- c("#3B4992", "#EE0000", "#008B45", "#631879", "#E69F00", "#008280",
         "#BB0021", "#5F559B")

ui <- page_sidebar(
  sidebar = sidebar(
    radioButtons("link", "linkage", choices = c("complete", "average", "single", "ward.D2")),
    sliderInput("K", "cut into K clusters", min = 1, max = 8, value = 3)
  ),
  layout_columns(col_widths = c(7, 5),
    plotOutput("tree", height = "560px"),
    plotOutput("scatter", height = "560px"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  h <- reactive(hclust(D, method = input$link))
  output$tree <- renderPlot({
    hc <- h()
    heights <- sort(hc$height, decreasing = TRUE)
    cut_at <- if (input$K == 1) max(hc$height) * 1.05 else mean(heights[c(input$K - 1, input$K)])
    par(mar = c(2, 4, 3, 1), cex = 1.1)
    plot(hc, hang = -1, main = sprintf("%s linkage: cut at height %.2f", input$link, cut_at),
         xlab = "", sub = "", ylab = "merge height")
    abline(h = cut_at, col = "#EE0000", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
    if (input$K > 1) rect.hclust(hc, k = input$K, border = pal[1:input$K])
  }, res = 96)
  output$scatter <- renderPlot({
    cl <- cutree(h(), input$K)
    # colour clusters in the left-to-right order of the tree, to match the boxes
    ord <- unique(cl[h()$order])
    d$cluster <- factor(match(cl, ord))
    ggplot(d, aes(x1, x2, colour = cluster, label = id)) +
      geom_point(size = 7, alpha = 0.35) + geom_text(size = 4, colour = "black") +
      scale_colour_manual(values = pal) + coord_equal() +
      labs(title = sprintf("K = %d", input$K)) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }, res = 96)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Things to try:

- **Move the cut.** One tree gives every $K$ from 1 to 30. You choose $K$
  after the fit, by choosing the height of the cut.
- **Look for a long vertical gap.** With Ward linkage, the three groups merge
  far above everything else. A cut anywhere in that long gap gives the same
  three clusters, and here they match the true groups (one point off). This is
  the "longest vertical line" rule from the slides. Complete linkage also
  shows a gap at three clusters, but a shorter one, and its three clusters
  misplace 4 points.
- **Read heights, not left-to-right order.** Two leaves next to each other on
  the axis are not always close. Only the height where their branches join
  tells you how far apart they are.
- **Compare the linkages.** Single linkage makes a flat, chained tree: below
  the top merge, the merge heights are small and close together, so there is
  no clear place to cut. Ward's merge heights are on another scale (they grow with the
  increase in WSS), so compare the shape of the trees, not the numbers.

## Things worth remembering

- **Lloyd's algorithm never increases WSS**, so it always stops. But it stops
  at a **local** minimum. Use `nstart = 25` or more, and set a seed.
- **Distance depends on units.** A variable with a large spread dominates,
  even when it carries no information. Standardize first.
- **No single tool chooses $K$.** The silhouette cannot say "no clusters". The
  gap statistic gives up when groups overlap. Use them together, and look at
  the clusters.
- **k-means finds round groups of similar size.** For long, curved, or nested
  groups, it gives a confident but wrong answer. Hierarchical clustering with a
  suitable linkage, or the mixture models of Class 8, can do better.

thyroid patients.
